verdict.rationale: Homebrew is a package manager that collects user data through analytics, so an AI-training privacy question is a fair axis. However, the evidence contains no policy or control about AI model training. The documented `brew analytics off` switch only disables anonymous aggregate usage analytics. That is an adjacent control, not an AI-training opt-out, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
